note: Contrarian Shark feedback on the Anchor Re-architecture Implementation Plan.

findings.topic: Silent data loss on rebuild for unconfirmed completed writes
findings.message: Under the proposed dual-write policy, if a crash occurs after the legacy write succeeds but before the CONFIRM marker is appended, the legacy store contains the mutated data but the journal only has the unconfirmed INTENT. Because the parity gate classifies this divergence as "OK-with-report" and the rebuild tool only consumes CONFIRMED events, rebuilding a deleted index.json will discard this valid, completed user mutation. This violates Success Criterion 3 by failing to recover a completed write from the journal. The reconciler should automatically promote/confirm such intents if the legacy store check passes, rather than relying on manual operator intervention while tolerating data-loss-vulnerable states as "OK".

findings.topic: ConPTY YES-branch deferral without North Star amendment
findings.message: If the ConPTY spike is successful (verdict YES), deferring PTY adoption to a follow-up effort (option ii) while leaving PTYs dashboard-owned violates Success Criterion 4 and the locked North Star Objective ("so the dashboard can restart without killing in-flight jobs or terminals"). A follow-up plan is only permitted if the spike refutes economic feasibility (verdict NO), or if a formal North-Star amendment is approved.

findings.topic: Windows permission conflicts on relocated data directory
findings.message: Running the supervisor service as `.\john` while the existing `anchor` dashboard service runs under a different account (e.g., LocalSystem) will cause Windows ACL permission conflicts in the shared `ANCHOR_DATA_DIR`. Since both processes must read and write to the same job records and event logs, the installer must ensure both services run under the same user account or explicitly configure inherited full-control ACLs on the relocated data directory.

findings.topic: Auth enforcement and client bootstrapping in a single wave
findings.message: Wave 9 combines the client-side bootstrapping changes (updating launchers to `/auth?token=`, setting the cookie) and the server-side auth enforcement in a single wave. Under the sequencing rule ("no auth flip ships in the same deploy as JS calling the flipped routes"), these must be deployed separately to prevent clients from receiving 401s during the rollout. Combining them in Wave 9 violates this safety rule and risks breaking the dashboard during deployment.
